kernels.spread_time: posteam_spread * exp(-4 * elapsed_share)   # spread scaled by clock decay
kernels.Diff_Time_Ratio: score_differential / exp(-4 * elapsed_share)   # lead divided by remaining-clock weight

implication_for_OU: The exp(-4*elapsed_share) kernel is the functional form our linear-decay mu_path lacked. At t=0: exp(0)=1 (full weight). At t=3600: exp(-4)=0.018. HALF-LIFE of the kernel = 3600*ln(2)/4 = 623s = 10.4min — the clock weight halves every ~10.4 minutes. Our OU theta half-life was 146-264 min (too slow); nflfastR bakes the clock into the FEATURE instead of the SDE. Alternative spec: OU with mu_path(t) = close * exp(-4 * t/3600) — exponential decay with the SAME 10.4-min half-life structure.
test_to_run: Replace OU mu_path with close * exp(-4 * t/3600) and re-run the quarter RVC. The kernel is the community-tested functional form; if it matches or beats our empirical attractor, the exponent -4 becomes a fit parameter (sweep -2..-8).
